title: ‘Digger’ Rakes in $1.2M Preview Box Office as Warner Bros. Faces Leadership Turmoil
body:
Tom Cruise’s latest action‑thriller, “Digger,” opened to a modest $1.2 million in domestic preview screenings on Thursday, a figure that underscores the precarious position of Warner Bros. Pictures as it navigates a leadership transition within its Motion Picture Group. The modest haul arrives at a time when the studio is scrambling to re‑establish its brand identity after a series of high‑profile missteps, and it comes just as Amazon’s MGM‑backed adaptation of Colleen Hoover’s bestseller “Verity” is poised to dominate the weekend box‑office conversation.

The preview earnings for “Digger” are a far cry from the blockbuster expectations typically attached to a Cruise vehicle. Industry analysts had projected a strong opening, citing the star’s proven draw and the film’s aggressive marketing campaign that highlighted its high‑octane set pieces and a gritty, subterranean premise. Yet the early numbers suggest that audiences are approaching the film with caution, perhaps wary of the franchise fatigue that has set in after a string of formulaic action releases across the industry.

Warner Bros. is currently undergoing a reshuffle at the top of its Motion Picture Group, a move that has been described as a “reset” aimed at revitalizing its slate and restoring confidence among investors. The transition follows a period marked by underperforming releases and a strategic pivot toward streaming that left the theatrical division in flux. “Digger” may be one of the first high‑profile titles to test the new leadership’s ability to rally the studio’s marketing machine and reconnect with cinema‑going audiences. The modest preview take could be an early warning sign that the re‑branding effort needs to be more aggressive, especially as rival studios line up tentpole releases for the holiday season.

Compounding Warner Bros.’ challenges is the looming competition from Amazon MGM Studios, which is set to release “Verity” this weekend. The adaptation of Hoover’s psychological thriller has generated considerable buzz on social media, driven by the author’s massive fan base and a strategic partnership with the streaming giant’s vast promotional resources. Early market research indicates that “Verity” could capture a sizable share of the weekend’s audience, particularly among younger viewers who have gravitated toward the novel’s intense, twist‑laden narrative. If the predictions hold true, “Verity” could eclipse “Digger” at the box office, further highlighting the shifting dynamics of audience preferences toward character‑driven, story‑rich fare over pure spectacle.

Critics who have previewed “Digger” offer a mixed verdict. While many commend Cruise’s committed performance and the film’s impressive practical effects, others point to a convoluted plot and a reliance on genre clichés that may limit its broader appeal. Trade publications note that the film’s pacing and tonal shifts could alienate viewers looking for a cohesive narrative experience. In contrast, “Verity” benefits from a tighter script and a marketing narrative that emphasizes its emotional stakes, which could translate into stronger word‑of‑mouth momentum once the film opens.

The $1.2 million preview figure, while modest, provides Warner Bros. with a data point to recalibrate its release strategy. The studio may need to consider expanding its international rollout, leveraging Cruise’s global star power, or augmenting its promotional spend to counter the competitive pressure from streaming‑backed releases. Additionally, the performance of “Digger” will likely influence the studio’s upcoming slate decisions, including whether to double down on action franchises or diversify into genres that have shown resilience in the current market.

Looking ahead, the weekend will serve as a litmus test for both studios. Warner Bros. hopes “Digger” can gain traction and demonstrate that traditional blockbuster formulas still have a place in a cinema landscape increasingly dominated by streaming giants. Meanwhile, Amazon MGM’s “Verity” aims to prove that literary adaptations, when paired with robust cross‑platform promotion, can capture the box‑office spotlight. The outcomes will not only shape the immediate financial results but also signal how the industry’s power balance may evolve as studios adapt to new leadership, changing audience tastes, and the ongoing convergence of theatrical and streaming distribution models.
